Province isolation stocks 360 Ituri, 519 Nord-Kivu, 76 Haut-Uele, 15 Tshopo and 10 Bas-Uele close to the printed national 980. A national confirmed/suspect split and national capacity denominator are not published.

Nord-Kivu prints 84.2% occupancy as 315/374, while the isolation census is 519; the generic all-census rate is withheld. Printed confirmed 84.2% (169/209) is 80.9% arithmetically, and printed suspected 84.2% (146/165) is 88.5%; the challenge paragraph separately prints 88.5%. The 156 patients outside CTE/CT plus 315 bed-counted patients sum to 471 rather than 519, and 156/519 is 30.1% rather than the printed 33.1%. Different/incomplete denominators remain unresolved.

Haut-Uele prints 49.7% occupancy with 54/153, which is 35.3% arithmetically; the census is 76, and 76/153 would round to 49.7%. The source explicitly flags incoherent care data, so the generic rate is withheld, preserving both printed counts.

Tshopo prints 27.8% occupancy as 10/36, while the isolation census is 15. Six confirmed plus four suspected patients classify ten, leaving five unspecified; the generic all-census rate is withheld rather than replacing the source with 15/36.

Six province rows sum to the printed national line 24,717/30,891 (80.0%); Sud-Kivu unavailable, not zero. Mutwanga (956 contacts) and Makiso-Kisangani did not submit follow-up reports; their denominator inclusion is not resolved by the source.

The national isolation stock changes from 1066 at SR145 to 980 at SR146 (-86). Printed admissions/exits are incomplete and previous province stocks were not published in SR145, so no incident-admission or causal interpretation is inferred.
